title: Incremental Trace Hook Bridge and Per-slice Anomaly Threshold Tuner
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, incremental "trace hook bridge" that can enrich span/trace payloads with runtime context and forward sampling hints to the anomaly detector. Combine this with a per-traffic-slice anomaly-threshold tuner that adapts burn-rate alert thresholds based on recent baseline drift and inferred request criticality.

Motivation: Current SLO alerts frequently generate noisy pages for multi-tenant flows that have transient, non-customer-impacting latency spikes. Our intent is to reduce noisy paging while preserving sensitivity for real regressions by (1) surfacing richer trace attributes early in the pipeline, (2) letting the anomaly detector adapt thresholds per-slice, and (3) exposing a runaway-suppression policy for low-impact slices during quiet windows.

Scope:
- Implement trace-hook bridge as a minimal sidecar hook that adds: route metadata, cached KV hints, sampling provenance, and request-priority tags.
- Enrich metric/log pipeline: map span attributes to the metrics platform ingestion schema and emit lightweight span-derived metrics for rolling baseline calculation.
- Build an anomaly-threshold tuner service that calculates per-slice dynamic thresholds and writes threshold updates to the alerting engine via the existing alert-config API.
- Provide a Console dashboard with per-slice SLI decay curves, tuned-threshold overlays, and a visual diff of before/after alert noise (30d).
- Rollout canary to 10% of traffic, then 50%, with an automatic rollback if pager volume increases >20% or error rate worsens by >0.5% absolute.
acceptance_criteria: Trace-hook bridge deployed to canary service and emits enriched span attributes to tracing pipeline
Anomaly-threshold tuner computes and persists per-slice thresholds for at least 3 slice dimensions (route, model_variant, customer_tier)
Alerting engine respects updated thresholds and burn-rate calculations use tuned thresholds during canary
Console dashboard shows baseline vs tuned thresholds and includes a noise-reduction metric (pages/hour) with historical comparison
Canary rollout plan executes with automatic rollback conditions and no customer-facing SLO regressions observed during canary
implementation_notes: Prototype implemented as two small components: trace-hook as a LightGo sidecar (low-latency), threshold-tuner as a Python service using the anomaly-detector lib. Use Redis for short-lived threshold cache and Kafka topic 'slo-tuner-updates' to persist changes before writing to alert-config. Key trade-offs: keep trace-hook CPU under 1% tail for p99 paths by sampling attributes and using probabilistic span extension. Avoid changing core tracer SDK to reduce upgrade blast radius.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Feature flag + internal canary (5 internal services) for 72 hours; collect metrics and pagers
Stage 2: Canary to 10% of production traffic for 24 hours; monitor pages/hour, p99 latency, error-rate delta
Stage 3: Expand to 50% for 48 hours if stability criteria met
Stage 4: Full rollout with 24h observation and soft-guard rollback if page volume increases > 20%
Post-rollout: 7-day observation window and capture runbook incidents for any residual noise
test_plan: Unit tests for trace-hook attribute extraction (edge cases: missing headers, truncated spans)
Integration test: synthetic probe that injects latency bursts to verify tuner raises thresholds appropriately
Load test: run trace-hook at 5x production QPS to measure CPU and latency overhead
Chaos tests: simulate downstream ingestion lag and ensure tuner degrades gracefully (no threshold thrashing)
monitoring_dashboards: Console: SLO per-slice view (latency p50/p95/p99) with tuned-threshold overlay
Alerting: pages/hour by slice and global burn-rate trend
Trace pipeline: hook processing latency histogram and dropped-attribute count
Tuner health: cache hit ratio and last-successful-write-to-alert-config
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ava Martinez: Spike complete. Prototype sidecar implemented; basic attribute enrichment works. Observed ~0.4% median p95 tail increase at 5x QPS when running full enrichments. Planning to add probabilistic attribute sampling to reduce cpu.
2025-02-18 - Miles Chen: Design review held with Platform and SRE. Decision: keep enrichment idempotent and opt-in via route config. SRE requested an opt-out list for high-volume internal routes.
2025-02-24 - PR opened: gh-2435. Initial tuner MVP computes thresholds using 14-day rolling MAD baseline. Needs integration test for bursty traffic patterns.

2025-03-01 - QA: Synthetic probe shows tuner correctly raises thresholds for periodic batch jobs but did not suppress pages for a short-lived downstream outage; investigating alert-config write cadence and rate-limiter behavior.

2025-03-05 - Miles Chen: Canaries scheduled for 2025-03-10 in cycle window. Remaining tasks: add per-slice quiet-hour weighting, final runbook draft, and SLO owner signoff. Marking blockers: none at this time.
